name-tag.scope: All five data resources inspected; Java-free Fabric resource registration is separate from the pack logic.
mechanics: Adds a shapeless name-tag recipe using paper and a metal-nugget tag, and a tick advancement unlocks that recipe.
An interaction advancement invokes a function that revokes itself and tags named entities. The scanned data resources do not themselves establish the catalogue's advertised entity-drop behavior.
risks: The recipe references the minecraft metal-nugget tag while a local name_tag tag is declared; verify the intended vanilla tag exists. Naming-tag scans and global advancement revocation can affect other players.
validation: Check recipe tag resolution, named-entity tagging, two simultaneous players, and whether any omitted overlay supplies the advertised drop behavior.

craftingtweaks.scope: Bulk resource/schema review of 988 data entries plus the complete load function; individual recipe balancing is not independently validated.
mechanics: Adds 260 stonecutting, 445 shaped crafting, 138 smelting, and 143 shapeless crafting recipes. They use ordinary recipe data consumed by Minecraft's recipe manager.
The load function grants all recipes to currently present players. No custom rendering or simulation fast path is involved.
risks: Changes crafting outputs and recipe search/load workload. Newly joining players and recipe conflicts require unlock/namespace checks.
validation: Validate every recipe against the target schema, item/tag existence and overlapping resource IDs; compare crafting outputs and reload errors.
craftingtweaks.fit: Content/quality-of-life data pack, not an FPS optimization.

mechanics: Replaces the creeper entity loot table with a gunpowder entry carrying count and looting-related settings. The file uses a modifier array on the entry.
risks: The exact loot-table schema must recognize modifier/type fields; do not assume the advertised counts are applied. Replacing the table can remove other vanilla or mod-added drops.
validation: Load against the target game schema and test creeper kills with different looting levels and other loot-table overrides.

craftables-datapack.scope: Schema/category review of 131 resources, complete load/tick functions, and representative recipes/unlocks.
mechanics: Adds recipes for items such as chainmail armor, ores, and normally unavailable equipment through standard shaped/shapeless/smelting/stonecutting formats.
Advancements unlock selected recipe groups. The load function prints a message; the registered tick function is empty.
risks: Changes item availability/economy. Recipe and ingredient formats vary between game versions, and an empty tick registration still has dispatch overhead.
validation: Validate target-version schemas and IDs, unlock triggers, resource override priority, and recipe outputs.
craftables-datapack.fit: Crafting content; not an FPS optimization.

woodworking.scope: Schema/category review of all 254 data entries and representative input/output recipes.
mechanics: Registers 239 stonecutting recipes and 15 shaped recipes for wood conversions such as stripping logs and making planks/slabs/stairs.
Uses the ordinary stonecutter/recipe-manager engine; no custom faster crafting engine exists in these resources.
risks: Changes available conversions and yields. Recipe duplication or balancing loops can create unexpected item gains.
validation: Check target schema, material IDs, yield consistency, duplicate recipes, and reload logs.

mechanics: Adds a shaped recipe with five string items in an X pattern, producing three cobwebs.
risks: Changes item availability and crafting economy; no hot-path optimization is present.
validation: Check recipe loading and the five-string/three-cobweb result.

dripstonerecipefix.scope: Both recipe and advancement resources inspected completely.
mechanics: Adds a shapeless conversion from one dripstone block to four pointed dripstones. An advancement unlocks the recipe on relevant inventory/recipe events.
risks: Uses plural recipe/advancement directories and legacy item-key formats in the inspected artifact; compatibility with the selected modern version is not established by catalogue matching.
validation: Check resource directory/schema recognition and crafting/unlock behavior on the target version.
dripstonerecipefix.fit: Recipe correction; not a performance algorithm.

crafting-refinements-blast-buff.scope: All four blasting recipes and corresponding advancement category inspected.
mechanics: Adds blast-furnace processing for raw copper/gold/iron blocks and sand to glass. Raw-block recipes specify 1600 cooking ticks and 6.3 XP; glass specifies 200 ticks and 0.1 XP.
Advancements unlock the recipes from material acquisition or recipe knowledge.
risks: Changes processing availability and rewards rather than computational cost. Target-version recipe-unlock fields require validation.
validation: Verify load schemas, unlocks, cook duration, fuel use, item conservation, and XP outputs.
crafting-refinements-blast-buff.fit: Gameplay recipe extension, not an FPS optimization.

get-my-blocks-back.scope: Bulk schema review of 197 shaped recipes and representative slab/stair conversions; all balancing combinations not manually audited.
mechanics: Adds recipes converting slabs and stairs back into their full block materials. Representative conversions use two slabs for one block and four stairs for three blocks.
Entire mechanism is declarative shaped-recipe loading; there are no JVM rendering/ticking hooks.
risks: Changes crafting economics and can interact with other modified-yield recipes. Resource/item coverage varies with game version.
validation: Check schema/IDs and conservation across forward/back conversions, including other recipe packs.
get-my-blocks-back.fit: Crafting convenience, not a performance feature.

simple-sugarcane.scope: All four resource roles inspected; the large optional block-ID list was examined by schema/category rather than every ID's behavior.
mechanics: Adds a broad optional-block tag to minecraft:supports_sugar_cane_adjacently. Ordinary sugar-cane support rules then accept many neighboring blocks where water was required.
A load function creates an initialization scoreboard marker and emits a message only once.
risks: Changes plant survival/growth rules. Extending the support tag does not necessarily cover every sugar-cane check or game version.
The multiline message and continued command syntax must be interpreted correctly; command counting alone is not semantics.
validation: Check target tag consumers, plant survival/growth on dry terrain, optional missing IDs, reload, and initialization.

crafting-refinements-six-stairs.scope: Schema/category review of all 97 shaped stair recipes and representative complete entries.
mechanics: Overrides stair recipe IDs in the minecraft namespace using the familiar six-block staircase pattern, changing the result count to six stairs.
risks: Resource priority determines which recipe wins. Modified stair yields interact with stair-to-block conversion packs.
validation: Check all output counts, item/recipe IDs, pack priority, and round-trip material conservation.
crafting-refinements-six-stairs.fit: Recipe yield change, not performance optimization.

crafting-refinements-recipe-rebalance.scope: Category/schema review of 18 data entries and representative complete recipes.
mechanics: Adds unpacking recipes such as bamboo blocks to nine bamboo, honeycomb blocks to nine honeycomb, and packed ice to nine ice, plus adjusted shaped recipes and unlock advancements.
risks: Changes item conversion ratios and availability. Combined recipe overrides can create loops or different balancing.
validation: Compare every configured input/output ratio, unlock schema, recipe priority, and conversion loops.

norollback.scope: All seven data entries and the one empty loader-wrapper class inspected.
mechanics: On load, schedules commands disabling player and elytra movement checks. Includes both legacy and newer gamerule spellings/directory layouts for different versions.
risks: Disables server movement validation, changing gameplay/authority. Unsupported gamerule names or directory layouts can fail on the selected version.
validation: Determine active resource layout and valid gamerule IDs for the game version; test movement correction and reload persistence.
norollback.fit: Server rule change, not rendering optimization.

ly-clumps.scope: All function bodies reviewed, plus config-dialog schemas; complete GUI layout not runtime-tested.
mechanics: Creates scoreboard-based configuration and runs merge/optional instant-pickup functions every tick.
A merge pass selects an orb anchor, selects nearby orbs, adds their Value through scoreboard operations to the nearest target orb, resets target age, and kills merged sources.
Instant pickup reads orb Value into command storage, uses a macro to add XP points to the nearest player, plays pickup sound, and kills the orb. Radius/toggles are changed through dialogs.
risks: Direct xp add bypasses the ordinary orb collection path, including any mending/pickup side effects. Selector execution position is crucial to target choice and total XP conservation.
Repeated entity scans/command dispatch have a cost; fewer orbs are not proof of net speedup. Age resets change despawn behavior, and scoreboard values can overflow.
validation: Prove XP conservation and selector context for overlapping orbs/players; check mending, age, spectator handling, multiple dimensions, and command workload at high orb counts.
ly-clumps.fit: Entity-count reduction with gameplay changes; not a drop-in equivalent optimization.

mechanics: Registers a tick function that repeatedly gives all players 60 seconds of night vision at amplifier 10 with hidden particles.
risks: Deliberately changes lighting perception and effect state. Reapplying an effect every tick adds command/entity work.
validation: Check effect duration/persistence, all dimensions, particle behavior, and tick overhead.
night-vision-datapack.fit: Permanent visual/effect change; not unchanged-visuals optimization.

mechanics: Each tick, executes a fill around every player over a 21 by 16 by 21 block volume, replacing nonpersistent leaves with distance seven by air using destroy behavior.
risks: Forces leaf destruction rather than preserving random decay timing. Scanning 7056 candidate positions per player per tick plus block updates/drops can add substantial work.
validation: Compare leaf criteria/drops and decay behavior; profile overlapping players, forest density, block updates, and unloaded regions.
fast_leaf_decay.fit: Faster gameplay decay, not necessarily faster computation.

no-piglinbrutes.scope: All six data entries and empty loader wrapper inspected.
mechanics: Registers a legacy-layout tick function that kills all piglin brute entities and a load message. Advancements provide pack branding/information.
risks: Removes mobs/gameplay. Legacy resource directories and entity kill drops must be checked on the chosen version.
validation: Check function registration, brute creation/removal, loot, dimensions, and reload messages.
no-piglinbrutes.fit: Mob-removal gameplay pack, not equivalent optimization.

no-more-explosions.scope: All function bodies and settings resource roles reviewed.
mechanics: Uses scoreboard settings for TNT, TNT minecarts, creepers, crystals, and fireballs. Tick commands remove selected explosive entities or set creeper explosion radius to zero.
Load initializes missing settings and exposes command-driven clickable controls; a notice dialog describes the pack.
risks: Changes explosion/gameplay results rather than speeding the original algorithm. Entity NBT names/types and kill/damage side effects are version-sensitive.
Repeated global entity/NBT scans can cost CPU; cancellation-by-removal can still create item drops or other side effects.
validation: Verify each explosive category, NBT predicates, settings persistence, drops, command permission, and tick overhead.
no-more-explosions.fit: Explosion suppression rule pack, not exact performance optimization.

visually-waxed-golems.scope: Function/advancement/team mechanics reviewed; associated visual assets or resource-pack shader/model integration remains pending.
mechanics: Uses advancements for wax/scrape events, a waxed scoreboard team, and a trigger objective for manual updates.
Team assignment identifies waxed copper golems by next_weather_age equal to -2; scrape/update functions remove or add membership. Uninstall removes the team and objective.
risks: Entity team membership is shared gameplay state and can overwrite other uses. Team assignment alone does not establish the advertised texture difference without tracing the associated visual mechanism.
validation: Inspect visual assets, event predicates and target-version NBT; check existing teams, wax/scrape, dimension scope, and uninstall cleanup.
visually-waxed-golems.fit: Visual content distinction; not an optimization.

disable-spawner-mob-spawns.scope: All four data resource roles reviewed.
mechanics: A legacy-layout load function sets spawnerBlocksEnabled to false. Advancement resources supply pack information.
risks: Changes spawner gameplay and depends on the gamerule and function-layout support in the selected game version.
validation: Check gamerule recognition, function registration, spawning before/after reload, and persistence after uninstall.
disable-spawner-mob-spawns.fit: Disables gameplay work; not equivalent optimization.

mechanics: Each tick, checks whether a position 161 blocks along positive Z from each player is loaded. If it is, deals 0.1 damage to the player.
risks: Loaded server positions are not a reliable measurement of a client's render distance; spawn/forced chunks and other players can satisfy the test.
The mechanism punishes players and does not directly set client distance or accelerate rendering.
validation: Test forced/spawn chunks, nearby players, server view/simulation settings, and whether the check corresponds to any intended client condition.

mechanics: Every tick, sets the life NBT field of ordinary and spectral arrows to 6000, making arrows reach the ordinary expiry criterion when that field is used.
risks: Changes arrow persistence/recovery. The command applies to all matching arrows, not explicitly only grounded arrows; actual effect depends on vanilla's lifetime update path and NBT schema.
validation: Check airborne/grounded arrows, pickup, lifetimes, target-version NBT types, and entity scan overhead.
instant-arrow-despawn.fit: Projectile removal policy, not equivalent optimization.
